id: So So Modern - Light Years EP Relief Show (All Ages - 3pm)-Newtown Community Centre, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: So So Modern - Light Years EP Relief Show (All Ages - 3pm)
long_description:
*** AA SHOW SOLD OUT *** NO DOOR SALES SORRY ***

SET TIMES:
3:00PM - DOORS
3:30PM - WELCOMER
4:15PM - SO SO MODERN

Pōneke post-punks So So Modern celebrate the release of their new EP Light Years, their first new material in 13 years, with a whānau-friendly, all-ages matinee show at their local Newtown Community Centre.

So So Modern built their reputation as one of Wellington’s most renowned live acts through relentless touring alongside international acts like Foals, CSS, Deerhoof and Dirty Projectors. After an extended break the band returned to play new songs alongside old at Camp a Low Hum 2024 and more recently Great Sounds Great.

Now, this special all-ages show offers a chance for all generations of music fans to see So So Modern live, with the added bonus of being a great way to avoid election anxiety (ENROL TO VOTE).

With a sound built on complex and chaotic layering of synthesisers, guitars and rhythm, the band’s latest release Light Years shows clarity, restraint and simplicity. The limited 12” vinyl release by Flying Nun and Holiday Records is accompanied by the illuminating artwork by Lily Paris West on two exclusive colourways. To mark the occasion the band are also selling the first ever So So Modern T-shirts, featuring an exclusive design by all-time friend and national treasure, Toby Morris.

Ear plugs will be provided but bringing your own ear protection is encouraged, especially for under-5s.

Under 14s must be accompanied by a guardian.

Capacity is strictly limited, don’t miss out.

See separate listing for the R18 6:30pm show the same day.

id: Kina:suttsu (Japan) | Vegetable.animal.machine-Pyramid Club, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Kina:suttsu (Japan) | Vegetable.animal.machine
long_description:
Pyramid Club is excited to present Japanese musician, performance and visual artist Kina:suttsu. Utilising saxophone, electronics, noise, and field recordings, Kina:suttsu creates immersive performances that blur the boundaries between ancient ritual and contemporary experimental music.

Since releasing her first album in 2005, she has performed and exhibited in Japan and internationally. Her releases include music on labels in the UK and France, including a cassette as NAVU and a collaborative release with Phil MFU, Zongamin, E-Da (ex Boredoms, Seefeel). She has recorded with legendary bassist Jah Wobble and released a live recording with Damo Suzuki. In 2021, she appeared in and composed the soundtrack for British filmmaker Daisy Dickinson’s short film Kaki no Shizuku, which was selected for the Los Angeles Film Awards.
-
vegetable.machine.animal (vma) is an interspecies improvisational trio led by drummer Kieran Monaghan, which transforms the electrical signals of living plants and fungi into sound, fusing modular synths and live percussion in performances that are spontaneous, rhythmic, and unpredictable. This is music as a living system - a real-time collaboration where non-human organisms shape the sonic outcome alongside human performers.


Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.

id: Ubuntu Cultural Conversations-The Undercurrent, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Ubuntu Cultural Conversations
long_description:
The Undercurrent presents Ubuntu Cultural Conversations!

The Ubuntu Cultural Conversation is an interactive and inclusive cultural event that explores how humanity is understood, expressed, preserved, and shared through diverse cultural perspectives. Through a combination of live music, poetry, storytelling, and open audience conversations, the event will create a space for meaningful dialogue, cultural exchange, reflection, and connection.

The programme will feature live musical performances by Ras Judah (Botswana), Mohamed Shemi (Tanzania), and friends, alongside poetry and opportunities for audience participation. Shared cultural food will further contribute to the spirit of hospitality, community, and connection that lies at the heart of Ubuntu.

The African concept of Ubuntu is often expressed through the powerful saying, “I am because we are.” Rather than placing individual achievement at the centre of social life, Ubuntu emphasises the importance of community, cooperation, reciprocity, and shared wellbeing. It encourages us to recognise the humanity in one another and to respond to the challenges faced by others with understanding, kindness, and support.

The philosophy of Ubuntu reminds us that our lives are enriched when we care for one another, celebrate our differences, and work collectively to create inclusive and connected communities. It offers an opportunity to reflect on what it means to be human and how our relationships with others shape the societies in which we live.

Saturday Nov 7
Doors 6:30pm
Start 7pm
$15

Tickets available online and at the door!

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

We’ll see you there ☆

id: Shonen Knife - Aotearoa Tour 2026-Meow, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Shonen Knife - Aotearoa Tour 2026
long_description:
Fist-pumping, fun-loving, “candy”-shouting punks, unite!

In the most southerly tour yet, this NOVEMBER Shonen Knife generously offer one of the most joyous live-music gifts people will ever receive, bringing their quirky, food-focused pop punk performance to the good folk of Ōtepoti, Ōamaru and Ōtautahi - in addition to their Te Whanganui-a-Tara and Tāmaki Makaurau.


“…a Shonen Knife gig is exactly what my soul has been crying out for. An electric and unashamedly fun, pop-punk masterclass. 2026 live show review, Leeds, UK - louderthanwar.com

Shonen Knife’s last Aotearoa tour in 2024 wowed enthusiastic audiences in Waiheke and Raglan, and this tour will be no different. In the interim, the band has toured through South America, TWO tours of the United States, multiple dates in Japan and more! Kicking ass and taking no prisoners, their innate energy you’ll catch is the best kind of infection!

Honestly - where would the world be without live shows that leave you happier and lighter than when you entered the gig On their current US tour, Shonen Knife felt the need for their uplifting magic in Florida; their review in www.19.com says “The thing I’ve always loved about Shonen Knife is the joy they bring to their music. It’s infectious. It lets us disconnect from the darkness around us” This reviewer was also impressed “by the long line already waiting to make purchases. It stretched down the lawn all the way to the seats. I joined the autograph line and got my fanboy moment and a photo with the band.” The world is made that much better by a band like Shonen Knife, and soon Aotearoa will also experience their unique pop-punk exuberance.

With the upcoming release on AUG 21 of their re-cut seminal 1992 album Let’s Knife in Australia/NZ via Valve/MGM, Naoko, Atsuko and Risa cut into the sugar lines of their current world tour to chop it all up in their favourite wonderland of Aotearoa.

In a world drowning in irony Lets Knife Re-Cut arrives like a neon lifesaver thrown from a punk rock speedboat. Shonen Knife remind us all that rock can still be heartfelt, silly and absolutely essential. Grab this one immediately, crank it loud, and prepare to smile until your face hurts because these songs were built to outlast every trend going. – (Jammerzine)

The album’s original success was famously due to Nirvana. In 1992 Kurt Cobain revealed his obsession with the Japanese trio, calling them ‘his favorite band’, seeking them out to open for Nirvana. Shonen Knife had never heard of the band, but eagerly took advantage of the opportunity. They quickly put together Let’s Knife out of their catchiest, funnest songs, recorded them in English and headed to the USA to open for Nirvana’s national tour.

id: Niced Up-Moon Bar, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Niced Up
long_description:
Kia ora koutou, we are pleased to be welcomed through the airlock of Moon Bar this November for our inaugural event. We are a new collective of selectors looking to get hips moving and contribute to the alive and kicking Welly scene. Expect silly, fun but considered multi-genre dance music.

What does 'Niced Up' even mean? First heard on a festival dancefloor from someone with an inability to conjure up anything more profound, it was used to describe the exact moment when everything had peaked exactly at the same time with no negative energy in sight. It's exactly where we intend to be on November 7th.

We know it is election night so there will definitely be reasons to laugh and cheer, or cry and wail, but this is best done with friends and backdropped by tunes, so we think we’ve got you covered. What’s more, it’s free entry all night long!

We can't wait to see ya, bring your friends, bring your Whānau.

id: Raphael House Steiner School Fair - Outdoor Music Stage-Raphael House Steiner School, Lower Hutt, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Raphael House Steiner School Fair - Outdoor Music Stage
venue: Raphael House Steiner School, Lower Hutt, Wellington
long_description:
Get ready for a fantastic day of live music at the annual Raphael House Steiner Fair Outdoor Music Stage! Celebrating the diversity and creativity of Aotearoa’s music scene, this year’s lineup brings together an exciting mix of heavy riffs, alternative rock, underground sounds and captivating solo performances. Featuring Stretch to Mould, Damiasharko, Hexxer, Undies, Datu Beech, Athena Clark with Cyan Ye and Vince Cabrera, there’s something for every music lover. Come along, support local musicians, soak up the festival atmosphere and enjoy a brilliant day of live music, community spirit and family-friendly fun!

Wellington rock trio Stretch to Mould bring hard-hitting riffs, powerful vocals and dynamic musicianship to the stage. Expect energetic alternative rock with plenty of intensity and a sound built for live performance.

The solo project of Haylee Hailwood, guitarist and vocalist of Wellington grungegaze band Cruelly, Damiasharko explores a gentler, more intimate side of her songwriting. Expect atmospheric sounds, heartfelt emotion and an alternative edge.

Wellington’s hexxer delivers adventurous alternative rock that blends gritty guitar work, experimental songwriting and unexpected musical turns. Balancing intensity with atmosphere, Hexxer offers a compelling dose of the capital’s independent rock sound.

Undies, (3/5 of Wellington favourites Underwire), serve up catchy indie rock with a punchy, energetic live sound. Mixing alternative rock with surf-punk attitude, garage-rock grit and ska influences, they bring infectious melodies and plenty of personality to the stage.

A familiar face in Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s music community, Datu Beech brings experience across multiple projects and genres, including emo outfit Crying Club and his work with Hunter Jackson. Look forward to a performance showcasing the creativity of Wellington’s interconnected music scene.

Ex-student Athena Clark joins the lineup with a performance celebrating the talent and individuality of Aotearoa’s local music scene. A welcome addition to a diverse programme of artists and sounds. She is supported by Cian Ye, a talented guitarist and singer.

Pink Shoggoth is the solo project of Upper Hutt musician Vince Cabrera, who creates distinctive instrumental music using acoustic bass, blending melodic, ambient and cinematic qualities. His thoughtful, understated approach offers a chance to slow down and appreciate the expressive possibilities of an unconventional solo instrument. Vince sings songs about myths and legends around the world.

Free entry!
Come make a candle and shoot an arrow!!
